Anna L: Heads-up — reproducible memory creep on long-context contbatch runs. Seen across 2 GPUs, appears correlated with repeated KV slot churn when batches merge/split frequently. (start)
Matt R: Can you paste the flamegraph/profile you captured?
Anna L: Pasted below — main hotspots in kv_store::evict_if_needed and in a new path kv_copy_on_kernel_switch. Also a bursty tail in continuous_batch::merge_wait.
Sasha P: Interesting. I saw similar in yesterday's perf run. My quick stack:
```
kv_store::evict_if_needed -> kv_frag_reclaim -> memcpy(kv->dst)
continuous_batch::attempt_merge -> head_of_line_wait -> schedule_rescue
kernel_selector::switch_kernels -> kv_copy_on_kernel_switch
```
Ben T: That kernel switch bit is suspicious. If we recompile kernels (or change attention tiling) mid-request we might be materializing KV tensor copies, which forces eviction cycles.
Ciara M: Do we have measurement for reuse ratio? i.e., fraction of KV slots reused across contiguous batches vs created new?
Anna L: Yes — I ran a 10k-step long-ctx sim. Reuse ratio drops from ~0.82 to 0.45 over time as fragmentation increases. Eviction rate increases and p95 latency drifts up ~18%.
Matt R: Any easy repro script? Could be useful to bisect whether it's contbatch merging logic or kernel switching.
Anna L: Minimal repro attached (ran on local docker). Pseudo log:
```
# simplified log excerpt
T=0 batch 1: allocate slots 0..15
T=1 merge(1,2): allocate slots 16..23
T=2 split(2): freed slots 16..19 (fragment)
... repeated merge/split pattern
mem_free ~6.2GB -> 4.0GB over 30m
kv_frag_ratio=0.21 -> 0.48
```
Sasha P: I also noticed the merge operation uses a naive placement which leaves small holes. Over long contexts those holes prevent reuse and force evicts.
Ben T: Proposal: introduce a "lifeline" counter per KV slot (age-based prefetch/gating). On merge, only allow cross-batch slot consolidation if lifeline > N and global frag < threshold.
Ciara M: Sketch:
```
# lifeline gating (concept)
for slot in merge_candidates:
  if slot.lifeline < LIFELINE_MIN or kv.frag_ratio > FRAG_THRES:
    postpone_merge(slot)
```
Ben T: Also add a light defragment pass that runs opportunistically when GPU load < 30% rather than during hot merges — copy cost amortized.
Anna L: That could help. Concern: extra copies increase immediate latency. We need a heuristic to avoid H-O-L blocking: if merge waits, it should decline rather than block the head batch.
Matt R: Right — avoid head-of-line. If a merge would block the head for >X ms, prefer to spawn a shadow merge or schedule after head finishes. Add metrics to measure merge_wait_time.
Sasha P: I ran a quick experiment toggling merge-on-schedule vs immediate-merge. Immediate-merge had 12% better throughput but 2.2x higher tail latency and memory churn. Scheduled-merge reduced evictions by ~30%.
Anna L: Good data. Can we gate merges behind kernel-selection stability as well? If kernel_selector reports upcoming kernel change (e.g., quantized path), avoid merge until steady.
Ben T: We can add a small API: kernel_selector::register_merge_guard(batch_id). If guard returns false, merges are delayed.
Ciara M: Action items:
- Anna: add lifeline counter + frag threshold prototype (PR)
- Sasha: run wide perf matrix with scheduled vs immediate merge (different workloads)
- Matt: add merge_wait_time metric + kernel-selector merge_guard hook
- Ben: prototype opportunistic defrag pass gated by GPU util
- repro-bot: run nightly regression job on long-ctx contbatch after PRs
repro-bot: CI job triggered: contbatch-kv-longctx-nightly (#3421) :white_check_mark:
Anna L: I'll open the PR with the prototype lifeline gating and some microbench numbers tomorrow. Recording this thread so we don't lose the context. :thumbsup:
Matt R: Thanks — if we can keep merge non-blocking by default we're golden. Let's sync on Friday for results.
